text.p: Tropical Cyclone 07B is moving westward across the Bay of Bengal and is expected to have top winds near 85 mph at the time of landfall in about 36 hours, which will occur in northern Andhra Pradesh, India. Heavy rain will likely lead to flash-flooding. Wind damage is also likely, especially near the coast. The storm will then move inland and weaken rapidly but will likely produce heavy showers and local flooding into south central India.

Tropical Cyclone Melanie-Bellamine is a very powerful storm with 120 mph top winds. The storm threatens only shipping in the southern Indian Ocean. It is centered near 11s/84e and drifting west southwest. It is expected to pick up foward speed but weaken in intensity, down to 75 mph by 48 hours.

Tropical Depression 36W, 400 miles southeast of Guam, is moving west at 2 mph, but is expected to pick up forward speed and turn toward Guam during the next 48 hours as top winds increase from 35 mph to near 70 mph. It will likely approach Guam as a typhoon.
Tropical Depression 37W is in the Philippine Sea, moving west northwest at 13 mph. This system may be a tropical storm before reaching the southern Philippines with wind and rain in 36-48 hours.
